I will keep my full 10.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation because that fits my land, my irrigation conditions, and the way I have farmed for many years. I have enough experience to manage both crops intensively, and with only two people in the household, I will keep the system simple and familiar rather than experimenting with a new crop. Since I have well irrigation, I will use improved seed and stable input levels to protect yield. For winter wheat, I will aim for a solid, high and steady stand with moderate-to-high fertilizer, several irrigations, and normal pest control, because wheat yield here depends heavily on water and nutrient timing. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same land and keep the turnaround fast. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, keep nitrogen a bit higher than wheat, irrigate when needed, and control weeds and insects with a few targeted pesticide sprays. I will use rotary tillage before wheat because I want a clean seedbed, and I will use no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest to save time, reduce labor pressure, and catch the summer planting window. My goal is reliable production, not unnecessary risk.
